sections.heading: The Scenario
sections.intro: The ruleset defines how models behave; the scenario defines the game. This is ours.

lines.text: Three minifigures per warband. Two or more players.
The game ends when only one warband still has a model on the battlefield.
That warband wins. No turn limit, no draw.
A scenario may restrict or extend the rules, never contradict them.
Before Turn 1: agree battlefield size, agree the Deployment Volume (W x D x H in UB), build forces, deploy, determine Priority.
End condition says when the game stops; victory condition says who wins.
Priority: every player rolls 1D6. Highest to lowest is the Activation Order; first place holds Priority. Reroll ties among the tied players only.
The Priority holder chooses once: activate now keeping their place, or cede Priority and drop to last while everyone else moves up.
Activate one unit at a time down the order. Skip players with none left. Continue until every unit has activated.
A unit activates exactly once per Turn. Its activation ends when the AP are spent or the player stops.
Every unit gets exactly 3 Action Points per activation. No unit ever gets more.
Spend AP in any legal order. Actions combine freely: Move / Move / Attack is legal, so is Rotate / Move / Attack.
End of Turn: resolve temporary effects, then scenario effects, then roll Priority again.
Forward: up to 4 UB (12 studs). 1 AP.
Backward: up to 4 UB (12 studs). 1 AP. Facing does not change.
Sideways: up to 3 UB (12 studs). 1 AP.
Rotate to any facing: 1 AP. No measuring.
No diagonal movement. Reach an off-axis square by combining legs; each leg is its own action and its own 1 AP.
Each move is measured on its own: 2 AP of movement is two moves of up to 4 UB, not one of 8 UB.
Measure along the direction of travel, from the face of the base that leads.
Wounded: at most 2 UB in any direction — 6 studs forward or back, 8 studs sideways. Everything else about the move is unchanged.
Obstacle up to 3 plate layers (1 brick): cross freely, no extra cost.
Obstacle 4 to 6 layers: climb for 1 extra AP per obstacle crossed. The climb does not extend the move's distance limit.
Obstacle 7+ layers: impassable without a slope, stair or ramp.
1 AP per weapon system attacking, however many dice it makes. Declare weapon, declare target, check Line of Sight, check range, roll, count Impacts, defender resolves them.
Line of Sight is physical: if you can see it, you can shoot it.
Any legally targetable part being visible from the attacker's viewpoint is enough.
Range = weapon length x 6. A 4-stud weapon reaches 24 studs; a 6-stud weapon, 36.
A functional muzzle is a visibly round opening on the weapon front. Square pieces are not muzzles.
Attack Dice = functional muzzles, one D6 each. Muzzle size changes strength, never the number of dice.
Attack Roll, per die: 4-6 scores one Impact, 1-3 nothing. A die can never score more than one.
Wounded attacker or Wounded weapon: for each Attack Die roll 2D6 and keep the LOWER, then read it as above. Same number of dice. Wounded states never stack.
Resolve each Impact on its own: pick the component hit, Geometry Check, Damage Roll, state change.
Impact Strength = muzzle size x 3. A 1x1 muzzle is 3, a 2x2 is 6, an NxN is 3N.
Resistance is not a statistic: it is the thinnest material the Impact must cross, in plate layers. Plate = 1, brick = 3. Empty space counts for nothing; walls are never added together.
Geometry Check: Strength below Resistance, the Impact stops and no die is rolled. Strength equal or above, continue.
Damage Roll, by the defender, one D6: 1-3 damages and advances the state one step, 4-6 does nothing. Note this reads opposite to the Attack Roll.
States: Operational, then Wounded, then Dead. Infantry shows it physically: upright, seated, removed. No tokens.
Wounded changes only the capability it provides — infantry moves shorter (INF-012), a weapon rolls the Wounded attack (CBT-015). Resistance, Strength and AP costs are untouched.
